title: Reactions of Acids with Carbonates
content:
# Reactions of Acids with Carbonates

## Learning Objectives

By the end of this lesson, you should be able to:
- Write equations for reactions between acids and carbonates
- Describe and test for the gas produced
- Explain observations for these reactions
- Use carbonate reactions to prepare salts

## Introduction

Carbonates and hydrogen carbonates react with acids to produce a salt, water, and **carbon dioxide gas**. The fizzing produced makes these reactions easy to identify.

## Key Concepts

### General Equations

**Carbonates:**
$$\text{Metal carbonate} + \text{Acid} \rightarrow \text{Salt} + \text{Water} + \text{Carbon dioxide}$$

**Hydrogen carbonates:**
$$\text{Metal hydrogen carbonate} + \text{Acid} \rightarrow \text{Salt} + \text{Water} + \text{Carbon dioxide}$$

### Examples with Carbonates

**With hydrochloric acid:**
$$\text{CaCO}_3 + \text{2HCl} \rightarrow \text{CaCl}_2 + \text{H}_2\text{O} + \text{CO}_2$$
$$\text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3 + \text{2HCl} \rightarrow \text{2NaCl} + \text{H}_2\text{O} + \text{CO}_2$$
$$\text{CuCO}_3 + \text{2HCl} \rightarrow \text{CuCl}_2 + \text{H}_2\text{O} + \text{CO}_2$$

**With sulfuric acid:**
$$\text{CaCO}_3 + \text{H}_2\text{SO}_4 \rightarrow \text{CaSO}_4 + \text{H}_2\text{O} + \text{CO}_2$$
$$\text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3 + \text{H}_2\text{SO}_4 \rightarrow \text{Na}_2\text{SO}_4 + \text{H}_2\text{O} + \text{CO}_2$$

**With nitric acid:**
$$\text{CaCO}_3 + \text{2HNO}_3 \rightarrow \text{Ca(NO}_3\text{)}_2 + \text{H}_2\text{O} + \text{CO}_2$$

### Examples with Hydrogen Carbonates

$$\text{NaHCO}_3 + \text{HCl} \rightarrow \text{NaCl} + \text{H}_2\text{O} + \text{CO}_2$$
$$\text{2NaHCO}_3 + \text{H}_2\text{SO}_4 \rightarrow \text{Na}_2\text{SO}_4 + \text{2H}_2\text{O} + \text{2CO}_2$$

Note: Hydrogen carbonates produce the same products but with different ratios.

### Ionic Equation

The key reaction is:
$$\text{CO}_3^{2-} + \text{2H}^+ \rightarrow \text{H}_2\text{O} + \text{CO}_2$$

Or for hydrogen carbonates:
$$\text{HCO}_3^- + \text{H}^+ \rightarrow \text{H}_2\text{O} + \text{CO}_2$$

### Testing for Carbon Dioxide

**Test:** Bubble the gas through limewater (calcium hydroxide solution)

**Positive result:** Limewater turns **milky/cloudy**

[DIAGRAM: Delivery tube from reaction flask bubbling gas into test tube of limewater, which turns cloudy]

**Equation:**
$$\text{CO}_2 + \text{Ca(OH)}_2 \rightarrow \text{CaCO}_3 + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$

The white calcium carbonate precipitate causes the milky appearance.

### Observations

| Reaction | Observations |
|----------|---------------|
| Marble chips (CaCO₃) + HCl | Fizzing/effervescence, solid dissolves, gas turns limewater milky |
| Copper carbonate + HCl | Green solid dissolves, fizzing, solution turns blue, limewater goes cloudy |
| Sodium carbonate + HCl | Solid dissolves, vigorous fizzing, limewater goes cloudy |
| Baking soda (NaHCO₃) + vinegar | Vigorous fizzing, typical "volcano" reaction |

### Common Carbonates

| Carbonate | Formula | Colour | Soluble? |
|-----------|---------|--------|----------|
| Sodium carbonate | Na₂CO₃ | White | Yes |
| Sodium hydrogen carbonate | NaHCO₃ | White | Yes |
| Calcium carbonate | CaCO₃ | White | No |
| Copper carbonate | CuCO₃ | Green | No |
| Zinc carbonate | ZnCO₃ | White | No |

### Everyday Examples

**Antacids:**
- Some indigestion tablets contain calcium carbonate
- CaCO₃ + 2HCl → CaCl₂ + H₂O + CO₂
- Neutralises excess stomach acid
- The CO₂ can cause burping!

**Baking:**
- Baking soda (NaHCO₃) reacts with acids in recipes
- CO₂ bubbles make cakes rise

**Cleaning:**
- Limescale (CaCO₃) fizzes with acidic cleaners

**Limestone weathering:**
- Acid rain attacks limestone buildings and statues
- CaCO₃ + acid rain → dissolves over time

## Worked Examples

**Example 1:** Write the equation for the reaction of calcium carbonate with dilute nitric acid. Include state symbols.

**Solution:**
$$\text{CaCO}_3\text{(s)} + \text{2HNO}_3\text{(aq)} \rightarrow \text{Ca(NO}_3\text{)}_2\text{(aq)} + \text{H}_2\text{O(l)} + \text{CO}_2\text{(g)}$$

---

**Example 2:** Describe what you would see when dilute hydrochloric acid is added to green copper carbonate powder.

**Solution:**
- Fizzing/effervescence/bubbles of gas
- The green solid dissolves/disappears
- The solution turns blue (copper chloride solution)
- The gas produced turns limewater milky/cloudy

---

**Example 3:** Describe the test for carbon dioxide gas and give the result.

**Solution:**
- Bubble the gas through limewater (calcium hydroxide solution)
- If carbon dioxide is present, the limewater turns milky/cloudy/white
- This is because calcium carbonate precipitate forms
- CO₂ + Ca(OH)₂ → CaCO₃ + H₂O

---

**Example 4:** Explain why calcium carbonate can be used as an antacid.

**Solution:**
- Calcium carbonate is a base (it can neutralise acids)
- Stomach acid contains hydrochloric acid
- CaCO₃ + 2HCl → CaCl₂ + H₂O + CO₂
- The carbonate neutralises the excess stomach acid
- This relieves the symptoms of indigestion
- The products (calcium chloride, water, CO₂) are harmless

## Common Mistakes

- **Mistake:** Forgetting that THREE products are formed
- **Correct:** Carbonate + acid → salt + water + CO₂

- **Mistake:** Confusing the test for CO₂ with the test for H₂
- **Correct:** CO₂ → limewater goes milky; H₂ → squeaky pop

- **Mistake:** Writing the wrong formula for carbonates
- **Correct:** Carbonate ion is CO₃²⁻, hydrogen carbonate is HCO₃⁻

## Practice Questions

1. Write the general word equation for the reaction of a carbonate with an acid. (1 mark)

2. Write balanced equations for:
   a) Calcium carbonate + hydrochloric acid (2 marks)
   b) Sodium carbonate + sulfuric acid (2 marks)
   c) Copper carbonate + nitric acid (2 marks)

3. Describe the test for carbon dioxide and state what you would observe. (2 marks)

4. A student adds dilute hydrochloric acid to copper carbonate.
   a) Write the equation for the reaction. (2 marks)
   b) Describe what the student would observe. (3 marks)

5. Write the ionic equation showing what happens to carbonate ions in acid. (2 marks)

6. Explain why limestone buildings are damaged by acid rain. (3 marks)

## Key Terms Glossary

| Term | Definition |
|------|------------|
| Carbonate | A compound containing the CO₃²⁻ ion |
| Hydrogen carbonate | A compound containing the HCO₃⁻ ion |
| Limewater | Calcium hydroxide solution, used to test for CO₂ |
| Effervescence | The production of bubbles of gas |

## Summary

- **Carbonate + Acid → Salt + Water + Carbon dioxide**
- **Hydrogen carbonate + Acid → Salt + Water + Carbon dioxide**
- Fizzing/effervescence observed (CO₂ gas released)
- **Test for CO₂:** Limewater turns **milky/cloudy**
- Ionic equation: CO₃²⁻ + 2H⁺ → H₂O + CO₂
- Uses: antacids, baking, cleaning limescale
- Colour changes: copper carbonate (green) → copper salt (blue)
